correctness.rationale: The star-transposition model is checked isomorphic to GP(12,5); graph distances split 24 vertices into two 12-vertex classes and the scale-three complex is exactly their join. Each factor is certified a connected orientable 12-vertex (12,36,24) torus by edge incidences, connected six-cycle links, and integral orientation propagation. The join Kunneth formula and graded factor-swap signs determine all three homology degrees, with no assumption of equivariant wedge splitting. The finite checker tests all 144 graph actions, proves the group is full through colored-neighborhood rigidity, computes torus Lefschetz and orientation traces, verifies all 15 product classes and irreducible inner products, and independently matches the full 5,328-face signed Lefschetz number for each element.

value.rationale: The canonical 24-vertex star-transposition/Nauru graph has an already known rare mixed-dimensional scale-three Rips homotopy type (join of two tori), making the equivariant structure of its three homology degrees a motivated and previously unresolved precise invariant. The result distinguishes a globally invariant third-homology line from fourth homology without fixed classes, and a top-degree bipartition-sign module; these are not implied by ordinary homology dimensions and provide a natural symmetry refinement of a documented graph-metric persistent topology case.
